questions.enonce_markdown: Draw a large and neatly labelled diagram of the kidney nephron. *(7 marks)*
Describe the formation of urine in humans. *(7 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Urine is formed in the **nephrons** of the kidneys in three stages.

1. **Ultrafiltration (glomerular filtration)**: blood enters the glomerulus through the wide **afferent arteriole** and leaves through the narrower **efferent arteriole**, which creates **high hydrostatic pressure**. This forces water, glucose, amino acids, mineral salts (ions) and **urea** out of the blood through the capillary walls and the basement membrane into the **Bowman's capsule**. Blood cells and large protein molecules are too big and remain in the blood. The fluid formed is the **glomerular filtrate**.
2. **Selective reabsorption**: as the filtrate flows along the **proximal convoluted tubule**, **all the glucose and amino acids**, most of the **mineral salts** and much of the **water** are reabsorbed into the blood capillaries by **active transport** and **diffusion/osmosis**. More water is reabsorbed in the loop of Henle and in the distal tubule and collecting duct; the amount depends on the hormone **ADH**.
3. **Secretion** (tubular secretion): in the distal tubule, some unwanted substances such as excess ions and drugs are added to the filtrate.

The remaining fluid, containing **water, urea and excess salts**, is the **urine**. It flows through the collecting duct into the **pelvis**, then down the **ureter** to the **bladder**, where it is stored until it is passed out through the **urethra**.

questions.enonce_markdown: State the roles of the liver in homeostasis. *(6 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The liver helps to keep the internal environment constant in these ways (any six points):

1. **Regulation of blood glucose**: when the blood glucose level is high, the liver, under the action of **insulin**, converts the excess glucose to **glycogen** for storage; when it is low, it converts glycogen back to glucose under the action of **glucagon**.
2. **Deamination of excess amino acids**: removes the amino group to form **urea** (excreted by the kidneys) and the rest of the molecule is used for energy or converted to carbohydrate or fat.
3. **Detoxification**: breaks down **alcohol, drugs and other poisons** into harmless substances.
4. **Regulation of body temperature**: the many chemical reactions in the liver release **heat**, distributed to the body by the blood.
5. **Breakdown of old red blood cells** and storage of iron, forming **bile pigments**; the **destruction of hormones** keeps their level in the blood constant.
6. **Storage of vitamins** (A, D, B12), iron and minerals; regulation of the amount of **plasma proteins**, lipids and cholesterol in the blood.
